1	# Vision Dataset Workbench
2	
3	Vision Dataset Workbench is a local, CPU-friendly command-line foundation for organizing image datasets. It stores a small manifest beside the dataset, imports image metadata without uploading files, and reports basic dataset statistics.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	- Python 3.11 or newer
8	- No third-party runtime dependencies
9	
10	## Quick start
11	
12	```bash
13	python3 -m vision_workbench init ./workspace
14	python3 -m vision_workbench add ./workspace ./examples/cat.jpg --label cat
15	python3 -m vision_workbench summary ./workspace
16	```
17	
18	The manifest is written to `.vision-workbench/manifest.json`. Importing the same file twice is idempotent because records are keyed by the file content hash. Imports, batch writes, undos and plan creation are serialized by a single workspace lock and committed through the same write-ahead journal, so several local processes can operate on one workspace at once: every successful operation survives, concurrent imports of different content all land, and duplicate imports report `already present` once while keeping the first registration's source and label.
19	
20	A single-file `add` registers the file's full SHA-256 digest, byte size and
21	resolved absolute source path, and all three are read from the same stable
22	regular file: the source is checked before and after the read, and the read
23	itself is pinned to the confirmed file. If the source is rewritten, appended
24	to, truncated, deleted and recreated, or replaced by another file (even one
25	with identical content, size and modification time) while it is being
26	confirmed or read — or if the path vanishes, becomes a directory or a
27	symlink, or cannot be opened or read in full — the import fails with the
28	source path and the reason, and no sample is registered. Content that
29	happens to match an existing digest never masks such a failure. A source
30	path that is a symlink when the command starts is still followed and its
31	target imported.
32	
33	## Importing a directory
34	
35	A whole directory of images can be registered in one batch:
36	
37	```bash
38	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --label cat
39	python3 -m vision_workbench import-dir ./workspace ./examples --recursive
40	```
41	
42	(The shorter `import` alias is equivalent.)
43	
44	- Only regular files with an extension of `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.bmp`,
45	  `.gif` or `.webp` (matched case-insensitively) are candidates. Symlinks
46	  and other entry types never qualify; recursion stays on the top level
47	  unless `--recursive` is given and never descends through symlinked
48	  directories. Files that appear after the scan are left for the next
49	  import.
50	- Candidates are ordered by their path relative to the source directory,
51	  with `/` separators, compared by Unicode code point.
52	- Samples are identified by their full SHA-256 digest. When several
53	  candidates share content that the workspace does not yet know, only the
54	  sorted-first candidate is added; the rest report `duplicate`. Digests
55	  already in the workspace always report `duplicate` and keep their
56	  original source, label and revision history — the batch label never
57	  overwrites an existing record.
58	- `--label` applies only to genuinely new samples. Omitting it leaves
59	  them unlabeled; the empty string also means unlabeled; any other string
60	  is kept literally.
61	- The result is JSON: the candidate count, the number added, the number
62	  of duplicates, and every candidate's relative path, full digest and
63	  `added`/`duplicate` status in scan order. Empty directories and
64	  all-duplicate imports succeed with zero added.
65	- The batch is all-or-nothing: a missing or non-directory source, a
66	  directory that cannot be scanned, a candidate that cannot be read in
67	  full, or a candidate whose identity, size or modification time changes
68	  while it is read fails the whole import with the path and reason and
69	  leaves no new samples. With `--recursive`, a subdirectory that was
70	  confirmed as a real directory and is then replaced by a symbolic link —
71	  wherever the link points — likewise fails the whole import with the
72	  subdirectory's path, rather than following the link or skipping the
73	  directory; the link target's images are neither imported nor reported
74	  as duplicates, and directories that were symlinks from the start are
75	  still simply ignored. The batch commits through the same journal as
76	  single-file imports, so an interruption shows either the old state or
77	  the complete batch, and concurrent label batches are never lost.
78	
79	## Split plans
80	
81	A split plan divides every sample currently in the manifest into a
82	train/validation/test set. Plans are saved under
83	`.vision-workbench/splits/<name>.json` and never change afterwards.
84	
85	```bash
86	python3 -m vision_workbench split create ./workspace baseline \
87	    --seed 42 --train 0.6 --validation 0.2 --test 0.2
88	python3 -m vision_workbench split show ./workspace baseline
89	```
90	
91	- The three ratios must be finite numbers in `[0, 1]` that sum to exactly
92	  one; any of them may be zero. Decimals (`0.1`) and fractions (`1/3`) are
93	  both accepted and handled with exact rational arithmetic.
94	- Stratification guarantees that, for every class and for the dataset as a
95	  whole, each set's count differs from its proportional expectation by
96	  strictly less than one — even for classes with one or two samples.
97	- Assignments depend only on sample content digests, labels and the seed,
98	  so they are stable across import order, manifest ordering, workspace
99	  location and restarts. Samples are listed by digest in each set.
100	- Unlabeled samples (no label or an empty label) form their own stratum,
101	  reported under the empty-string key `""`; a real class literally named
102	  `unlabeled` is kept separate.
103	- Creating under an existing name reuses the plan only when the seed,
104	  ratios, sample identities and labels all match; otherwise it reports a
105	  name conflict and leaves the original untouched. Sample identities and
106	  labels are snapshotted from one complete manifest state, so a batch that
107	  changes several labels is seen wholly before or wholly after the plan,
108	  never half-applied. Concurrent creation of one name is atomic: exactly
109	  one request creates it, identical requests reuse it and differing
110	  requests conflict; plans with different names all save, and a plan is
111	  only ever read whole or reported as not found.
112	
113	## Exporting a split plan
114	
115	A saved split plan can be exported as a portable, offline ZIP package:
116	
117	```bash
118	python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip
119	```
120	
121	- The package contains `train/`, `validation/` and `test/` directories,
122	  each with the same numbered ImageFolder class directories (`class_01`,
123	  `class_02`, ...), plus a UTF-8 `manifest.json`. Samples are stored as
124	  `<set>/<class>/<full-sha256><source-extension>`.
125	- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
126	  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
127	  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
128	  writes to the workspace.
129	- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
130	  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
131	  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
132	  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
133	  paths are written.
134	- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
135	- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
136	  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
137	  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
138	  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
139	  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
140	- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
141	  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
142	  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
143	- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
144	  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
145	  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
146	  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
147	  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
148	  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
149	  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
150	  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
151	  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
152	  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
153	  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
154	- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
155	  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
156	  ```bash
157	  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
158	      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
159	  ```
160	  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
161	  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
162	  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
163	  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
164	  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
165	  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
166	  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
167	  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
168	  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
169	  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
170	  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
171	  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
172	  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
173	  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
174	  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
175	  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
176	  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
177	  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
178	  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.
179	
180	  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
181	  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
182	  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
183	  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
184	  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
185	  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
186	  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
187	  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
188	  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
189	  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
190	  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
191	  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
192	  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
193	  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
194	  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
195	  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
196	  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
197	  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
198	  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.
199	
200	  Files unrelated to the
201	  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
202	  included. The plan still decides
203	  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
204	  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
205	  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
206	  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
207	  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
208	  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
209	  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
210	- The target must not already exist; it is written atomically, so a failure
211	  or interruption leaves no incomplete file. Concurrent exports to the
212	  same path are serialized and at most one succeeds.
213	- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
214	  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
215	  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
216	  do not matter.
217	
218	## Tests
219	
220	```bash
221	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
222	```
223	
224	## Batch label updates
225	
226	Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
227	UTF-8 JSON file:
228	
229	```json
230	{
231	  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
232	  "changes": [
233	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
234	    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
235	  ]
236	}
237	```
238	
239	- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
240	- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
241	  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
242	  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
243	  named `unlabeled`).
244	- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
245	  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
246	  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
247	  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
248	- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
249	  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
250	  number and writes no history.
251	
252	```bash
253	python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
254	python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
255	python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
256	python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
257	```
258	
259	Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
260	original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
261	`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
262	changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
263	conflict.
264	
265	`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
266	involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
267	changed. Failed batches never enter history.
268	
269	`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
270	actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
271	if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
272	the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
273	`already-undone`.
274	
275	Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
276	installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
277	the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
278	its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
279	runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
280	process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
281	prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
282	afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
283	are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
284	two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
285	win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
286	and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
287	never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
288	use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
289	apply.
290

- The export uses only the saved plan: its samples, labels, set
  assignments and recorded source paths. Later imports, batch label
  changes or undos never alter an exported package, and exporting never
  writes to the workspace.
- All sets share one class directory numbering, even when a class has no
  samples in a set. Chinese labels, labels containing path separators and
  labels differing only in case each keep a distinct identity in the
  manifest's label-to-directory mapping; no machine-specific absolute
  paths are written.
- An empty plan exports the three set directories and an empty manifest.
- Samples with no label are unlabeled. By default the whole export is
  rejected and the offending digest is reported; `--skip-unlabeled` skips
  them instead, listing the per-set skip counts in both the result and the
  manifest. Skipping never redistributes other samples. A real class
  literally named `unlabeled` is exported normally.
- Source files are streamed and verified against the saved content digest
  while copying: a missing, non-regular, unreadable or changed source
  fails the whole export with the sample digest and reason.
- A single sample at or above 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 bytes of uncompressed
  content) is written as a ZIP64 entry automatically; large and ordinary
  samples may coexist in one plan and one package, and the large entry is
  still streamed in fixed chunks, so exporting it never needs memory for
  the whole file. This also covers multi-gigabyte content that compresses
  well: the decision follows the uncompressed size, so a tiny resulting
  package is not rejected. Plans containing only smaller samples keep
  exactly the classic archive format, byte for byte — ZIP64 fields appear
  only in the entries that require them. The manifest, the result counts
  and the set/class layout are identical either way, and packages remain
  extractable with standard ZIP64-aware tools.
- `--source-dir` reads sample files from a directory tree instead of the
  recorded source paths, which is useful after moving the dataset:
  ```bash
  python3 -m vision_workbench export ./workspace baseline ./baseline.zip \
      --source-dir ./moved-dataset
  ```
  Every regular file under the directory and its subdirectories is
  considered (no extension filter, since files may have been renamed);
  symlinks and other non-regular entries are skipped and symlinked
  directories are never descended. Each exported sample must be matched
  to a file whose full SHA-256 matches the plan — a same-named file with
  different content does not qualify. When several files share content,
  the one whose `/`-separated relative path sorts first by Unicode code
  point is used. The selected copy is pinned to the actual read: the path
  is lstat()ed without following symlinks, opened without following a
  final symlink, and the opened descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be
  the exact regular file (same device and inode) captured during the
  lookup — the check covers the object that is really read, not just one
  look at the path before it opens. If the selected path is replaced
  after the lookup but before or while it is opened by another regular
  file — even one with identical content, size and modification time —
  or by a symlink, even one pointing at the original file, the whole
  export fails with the sample digest, the selected source path and the
  reason; no other same-content copy is substituted and the plan's
  recorded source path is not used as a fallback.

  The directory walk is itself pinned to directory descriptors rather
  than path strings: each directory is entered with `openat`
  (`O_NOFOLLOW` and `O_DIRECTORY`) relative to its parent's descriptor
  and verified with `fstatat`, and the confirmed root stays open for the
  whole export. A subdirectory that is a real directory when the walk
  first reaches it but is replaced by a symlink before it is entered,
  while its contents are read, after the lookup or while the package is
  copied fails the whole export with the changed directory's path and
  the symlink reason — whether the link points outside the specified
  directory, inside it, or at the directory moved to its new location,
  and at any nesting level. The link's target is never read, matched or
  packaged, even if it holds a file byte-identical to the planned
  sample; no other normal copy and no still-readable recorded source are
  substituted. Before each matched file is copied its ancestor
  directories are re-verified the same way, and after all samples are
  streamed every directory from the walk is verified once more before
  the ZIP is published, so the target ZIP is never created and no
  incomplete export file remains. Only entries that are already
  symlinks the first time the walk meets them are skipped, as before.

  Files unrelated to the
  plan are read (an unreadable file anywhere fails the export) but never
  included. The plan still decides
  sample identities, labels, set assignments and package file extensions;
  the lookup is used for this export only and is never written back. A
  missing or non-directory source, an unreadable directory or file, or a
  sample with no matching content fails the whole export with the path
  and reason; the package is byte-identical to a normal export of the
  same plan, options and content. For an empty plan (or when every sample
  is skipped) the directory only has to exist and be a directory.
- The target must not already exist; it is written atomically, so a failure
  or interruption leaves no incomplete file. Concurrent exports to the
  same path are serialized and at most one succeeds.
- Package bytes are deterministic for a given plan, options and source
  content: exporting at a different time, from a copied workspace or to a
  different path yields byte-identical ZIPs, and source modification times
  do not matter.

## Tests

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

## Batch label updates

Labels of already-imported samples can be changed in batches. A batch is a
UTF-8 JSON file:

```json
{
  "batch": "renumber-2026-01",
  "changes": [
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "cat", "new": "kitten"},
    {"sha256": "<full SHA-256 digest>", "old": "dog", "new": null}
  ]
}
```

- `batch` must be a non-empty string.
- `old` is the expected current label; `new` is the target label. Both may
  be a string or `null`; `null` and the empty string both mean *unlabeled*,
  any other string is taken literally (including Chinese text and a class
  named `unlabeled`).
- The whole batch is verified before anything is written: an unknown
  digest, a sample listed twice, a non-string/non-null label, a malformed
  file, or any sample whose current label differs from its expected old
  label rejects the entire batch with the offending record identified.
- Records whose target equals the current label are no-ops; if every
  record is a no-op, the batch reports `no-changes`, occupies no batch
  number and writes no history.

```bash
python3 -m vision_workbench label ./workspace <digest>      # current label
python3 -m vision_workbench batch ./workspace changes.json   # submit a batch
python3 -m vision_workbench history ./workspace              # successful batches
python3 -m vision_workbench undo ./workspace <batch-number>  # undo a batch
```

Submitting the same number with the same content again returns the
original result without re-modifying anything (list order and the
`null`/`""` spelling do not change the content), even if labels were
changed in the meantime. The same number with different content is a
conflict.

`history` lists successful batches in submission order: the samples
involved, their before/after labels, and the number of samples actually
changed. Failed batches never enter history.

`undo` restores the old labels of a batch, but only for samples the batch
actually changed and only when none of them was modified afterwards (even
if the label was changed back). Other samples' later changes do not block
the undo. Undo leaves a queryable record; repeating it reports
`already-undone`.

Imports, batch writes and undos are crash-safe: a write-ahead journal
installs the manifest and the history together, so after an interruption
the workspace shows either the old state or the complete new state with
its history — labels and their history never straddle the two. Recovery
runs under the workspace lock at the start of every operation, so a
process that already has the workspace open also completes a peer's
prepared transaction without reopening; a sample imported successfully
afterwards is never rolled back by that recovery. Concurrent operations
are serialized by the lock, so no successful import or batch is lost and
two batches modifying the same sample from the same old label cannot both
win. Summary, label and history queries each observe one complete state
and never report corruption from an in-flight write. Saved split plans are
never touched by imports, label changes or undos; plans created afterwards
use the current labels, and the same-name reuse/conflict rules still
apply.

338	# A resolver maps a full SHA-256 digest to the absolute path of the
339	# sorted-first regular file carrying that content, plus the file's
340	# identity (device, inode) captured during the lookup.  The copy opens
341	# that exact inode pinned through the open, so a swap after the lookup —
342	# another regular file, even with identical content, or a symlink, even
343	# one pointing at the original file — cannot be read in its place.
344	Resolver = dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]]

347	class _ScanResult(dict):
348	    """The digest resolver, also carrying every real directory seen.
349	
350	    Behaves as the plain digest-to-file resolver mapping, with an extra
351	    ``directory_ids`` attribute: each key is a ``/``-separated path
352	    relative to the root (``""`` for the root itself) and each value is
353	    ``(display path, device, inode)`` as observed during the walk.
354	    """
355	
356	    def __init__(
357	        self,
358	        files: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
359	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
360	    ) -> None:
361	        super().__init__(files)
362	        self.directory_ids = directories
363	
364	
365	def _scan_source_directory(root: Path) -> Resolver:
366	    """Walk ``root`` and map every digest to the sorted-first copy.
367	
368	    The directory and all its subdirectories are searched for regular
369	    files only: there is no extension filter, symlinks and other
370	    non-regular entries are skipped, and recursion never descends through
371	    symlinked directories.  Every regular file found is read in full and
372	    identified by its content digest; when several files share content,
373	    the one whose slash-separated path relative to ``root`` sorts first
374	    by Unicode code point owns the digest.  A directory that cannot be
375	    scanned, an entry that cannot be inspected or a file that cannot be
376	    read in full fails the export with the path and reason.
377	
378	    Every step is anchored to directory descriptors rather than path
379	    strings: a child is typed and entered with ``fstatat``/``openat``
380	    relative to the descriptor of the directory it was listed from, and
381	    each entered directory is pinned for the whole time its contents are
382	    processed.  A real subdirectory whose path is swapped for a symlink
383	    after it was listed but before or while it is entered therefore can
384	    never be followed — the open refuses the link and the export fails
385	    naming that directory — and a swap landing while its children are
386	    being read is detected when its path binding is re-checked after the
387	    children have been processed.  Only entries that are already
388	    symlinks when first listed are skipped, preserving the original
389	    convention.
390	    """
391	    try:
392	        root_fd = os.open(root, os.O_RDONLY | _O_DIRECTORY)
393	    except OSError as error:
394	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
395	    try:
396	        return _scan_tree(root_fd, root)
397	    finally:
398	        os.close(root_fd)
399	
400	
401	def _scan_tree(root_fd: int, root: Path) -> _ScanResult:
402	    """Walk the tree reached through the already-open, pinned ``root_fd``."""
403	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]] = {}
404	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] = {}
405	    try:
406	        root_status = os.fstat(root_fd)
407	    except OSError as error:
408	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {root}: {error}") from error
409	    directories[""] = (root, root_status.st_dev, root_status.st_ino)
410	    _walk_directory(root_fd, None, root, root, found, directories)
411	    files = {
412	        digest: (path, device, inode)
413	        for digest, (_, path, device, inode) in found.items()
414	    }
415	    return _ScanResult(files, directories)

418	def _walk_directory(
419	    parent_fd: int,
420	    name: str | None,
421	    display: Path,
422	    root: Path,
423	    found: dict[str, tuple[str, Path, int, int]],
424	    directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
425	) -> None:
426	    """Process one directory, anchored to a pinned descriptor.
427	
428	    ``name`` is the parent-relative basename; ``None`` marks the already
429	    open ``root`` whose descriptor is ``parent_fd``.  Any other
430	    directory is entered through :func:`_enter_subdirectory`, which
431	    pins the exact directory listed by the parent.
432	    """
433	    if name is None:
434	        directory_fd = parent_fd
435	        entered = False
436	    else:
437	        directory_fd = _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd, name, display)
438	        entered = True
439	    try:
440	        if entered:
441	            try:
442	                pinned = os.fstat(directory_fd)
443	            except OSError as error:
444	                raise ExportError(
445	                    f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}"
446	                ) from error
447	            rel = os.path.relpath(display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
448	            directories[rel] = (display, pinned.st_dev, pinned.st_ino)
449	        try:
450	            entries = list(os.scandir(directory_fd))
451	        except OSError as error:
452	            raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error
453	        for entry in entries:
454	            child_name = entry.name
455	            child_display = display / child_name
456	            try:
457	                status = os.stat(
458	                    child_name, dir_fd=directory_fd, follow_symlinks=False
459	                )
460	            except OSError as error:
461	                raise ExportError(
462	                    f"cannot inspect entry {child_display}: {error}"
463	                ) from error
464	            mode = status.st_mode
465	            if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
466	                # A symlink when first encountered: skipped, never read.
467	                continue
468	            if stat.S_ISREG(mode):
469	                digest, device, inode = _hash_regular_file_at(
470	                    directory_fd, child_name, child_display
471	                )
472	                rel = os.path.relpath(child_display, root).replace(os.sep, "/")
473	                current = found.get(digest)
474	                if current is None or rel < current[0]:
475	                    found[digest] = (rel, child_display, device, inode)
476	            elif stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
477	                _walk_directory(
478	                    directory_fd,
479	                    child_name,
480	                    child_display,
481	                    root,
482	                    found,
483	                    directories,
484	                )
485	            # Any other entry type is skipped as before.
486	        if entered:
487	            # The children are done and were all reached through this
488	            # pinned descriptor.  Re-prove the parent-relative name still
489	            # binds to this same directory: a symlink (or anything else)
490	            # swapped onto it while the children were being processed
491	            # must fail the export even though nothing was read through
492	            # that link.
493	            _assert_still_same_directory(
494	                parent_fd, name, display, directory_fd
495	            )
496	    finally:
497	        if entered:
498	            os.close(directory_fd)

501	def _enter_subdirectory(parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path) -> int:
502	    """Open a listed subdirectory relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin it.
503	
504	    The parent listed ``name`` as a real directory, so anything other
505	    than that same directory observed here means the path changed after
506	    the listing.  This is the first confirmation of the directory: no
507	    identity was recorded yet, so the fresh inspection itself sets the
508	    expectation the opened descriptor is then proved against.  A symlink
509	    swapped in at any point fails the export identifying ``display`` as
510	    a directory that changed into a symlink, and its target — outside
511	    the tree, inside it, or the moved original — is never touched.
512	    """
513	    return _open_confirmed_directory(
514	        parent_fd, name, display, expected=None, during_scan=True
515	    )

517	
518	def _open_confirmed_directory(
519	    parent_fd: int,
520	    name: str,
521	    display: Path,
522	    expected: tuple[int, int] | None,
523	    during_scan: bool,
524	) -> int:
525	    """Open ``name`` relative to ``parent_fd`` and pin the directory.
526	
527	    The single confirmation rule shared by the lookup and the package
528	    copy: the name is inspected with ``fstatat`` without following
529	    symlinks and then opened with ``openat`` using ``O_NOFOLLOW`` and
530	    ``O_DIRECTORY``; the descriptor is fstat()ed and proved to be the
531	    directory the inspection named.  ``expected`` carries the
532	    ``(device, inode)`` the binding must match — the identity recorded
533	    during the lookup when the copy re-checks an already confirmed
534	    directory, or ``None`` when the lookup confirms a directory for the
535	    first time and the fresh inspection itself is the expectation.
536	
537	    ``during_scan`` selects the phase the error messages report:
538	    failures while walking the tree say "during scan" and "cannot scan",
539	    failures while copying the package say "during export" and "cannot
540	    inspect".  A symlink swapped in at any point in this sequence fails
541	    the export identifying ``display`` and what it became; the link's
542	    target is never touched.
543	    """
544	    try:
545	        before = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
546	    except OSError as error:
547	        raise ExportError(f"cannot inspect directory {display}: {error}") from error
548	    if expected is None:
549	        expected = (before.st_dev, before.st_ino)
550	    if (
551	        stat.S_ISLNK(before.st_mode)
552	        or not stat.S_ISDIR(before.st_mode)
553	        or (before.st_dev, before.st_ino) != expected
554	    ):
555	        raise _directory_changed_message(
556	            display, before.st_mode, during_scan=during_scan
557	        )
558	    try:
559	        descriptor = os.open(
560	            name,
561	            os.O_RDONLY | _O_NOFOLLOW | _O_DIRECTORY,
562	            dir_fd=parent_fd,
563	        )
564	    except OSError as error:
565	        if error.errno in (errno.ELOOP, errno.ENOTDIR):
566	            # The path changed between the fstatat and the open; inspect
567	            # it once more to report the concrete reason.
568	            raise _directory_changed_error(
569	                parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
570	            ) from error
571	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
572	    try:
573	        opened = os.fstat(descriptor)
574	    except OSError as error:
575	        os.close(descriptor)
576	        raise _directory_access_error(display, error, during_scan) from error
577	    if not stat.S_ISDIR(opened.st_mode) or (
578	        opened.st_dev,
579	        opened.st_ino,
580	    ) != expected:
581	        os.close(descriptor)
582	        raise _directory_changed_error(
583	            parent_fd, name, display, during_scan=during_scan
584	        )
585	    return descriptor
586	
587	
588	def _directory_access_error(
589	    display: Path, error: OSError, during_scan: bool
590	) -> ExportError:
591	    """Report a directory that cannot be entered, naming the phase."""
592	    action = "scan" if during_scan else "inspect"
593	    return ExportError(f"cannot {action} directory {display}: {error}")

596	def _assert_still_same_directory(
597	    parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path, directory_fd: int
598	) -> None:
599	    """Re-check that ``name`` in the parent still names ``directory_fd``."""
600	    try:
601	        now = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
602	    except OSError as error:
603	        raise ExportError(f"cannot inspect directory {display}: {error}") from error
604	    try:
605	        pinned = os.fstat(directory_fd)
606	    except OSError as error:
607	        raise ExportError(f"cannot scan directory {display}: {error}") from error
608	    if (now.st_dev, now.st_ino) != (pinned.st_dev, pinned.st_ino):
609	        raise _directory_changed_message(
610	            display, now.st_mode, during_scan=True
611	        )

614	def _directory_changed_error(
615	    parent_fd: int, name: str, display: Path, during_scan: bool
616	) -> ExportError:
617	    """Build the change error, inspecting the swapped path once for the reason."""
618	    try:
619	        now = os.stat(name, dir_fd=parent_fd, follow_symlinks=False)
620	        mode: int | None = now.st_mode
621	    except OSError:
622	        mode = None
623	    return _directory_changed_message(display, mode, during_scan=during_scan)
624	
625	
626	def _directory_changed_message(
627	    display: Path, mode: int | None, during_scan: bool
628	) -> ExportError:
629	    """Fail naming the directory that changed and what it became."""
630	    phase = "during scan" if during_scan else "during export"
631	    if mode is not None and stat.S_ISLNK(mode):
632	        reason = "is now a symlink"
633	    elif mode is not None and stat.S_ISDIR(mode):
634	        reason = "was replaced by a different directory"
635	    else:
636	        reason = "no longer points to the directory being scanned"
637	    return ExportError(f"directory changed {phase}: {display} {reason}")

640	class _SourceAnchor:
641	    """Pinned view of the confirmed source tree, used while copying.
642	
643	    Holds the root descriptor for the whole export and the identity of
644	    every directory observed during the lookup.  Each verification
645	    re-derives directory bindings from descriptors (``fstatat`` and
646	    ``openat`` with ``O_NOFOLLOW``/``O_DIRECTORY``) instead of trusting
647	    path strings, so a real directory replaced by a symlink after the
648	    lookup — before a sample is opened, while it is read or between
649	    samples — fails the export even when the link leads to byte-equal
650	    content.  :meth:`verify_all` runs once more after every sample has
651	    been copied, so the package is never published when a binding
652	    changed.
653	    """
654	
655	    def __init__(
656	        self,
657	        root_fd: int,
658	        root: Path,
659	        directories: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]],
660	    ) -> None:
661	        self.root_fd = root_fd
662	        self.root = root
663	        self.directories = directories
664	
665	    def verify_file(self, source: Path) -> None:
666	        """Prove the root and all ancestor directories of ``source``."""
667	        parts = source.relative_to(self.root).parts[:-1]
668	        self._descend(tuple(parts))
669	
670	    def verify_all(self) -> None:
671	        """Prove the root and every directory recorded during the lookup.
672	
673	        A single descriptor-anchored traversal over the recorded
674	        parent/child structure opens each directory exactly once, so a
675	        tree of any depth costs one descent rather than one per
676	        directory.  Every open is an ``openat`` relative to the pinned
677	        parent, so a symlink swapped in at any level is refused.
678	        """
679	        self._check_root()
680	        children: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
681	        for key in self.directories:
682	            if not key:
683	                continue
684	            parent_key, _, name = key.rpartition("/")
685	            children.setdefault(parent_key, []).append((name, key))
686	        self._verify_children(self.root_fd, "", self.root, children)
687	
688	    def _check_root(self) -> None:
689	        _, root_dev, root_inode = self.directories[""]
690	        try:
691	            pinned_root = os.fstat(self.root_fd)
692	        except OSError as error:
693	            raise ExportError(
694	                f"cannot inspect directory {self.root}: {error}"
695	            ) from error
696	        if (pinned_root.st_dev, pinned_root.st_ino) != (
697	            root_dev,
698	            root_inode,
699	        ) or not stat.S_ISDIR(pinned_root.st_mode):
700	            raise _directory_changed_message(
701	                self.root, pinned_root.st_mode, during_scan=False
702	            )
703	
704	    def _verify_children(
705	        self,
706	        parent_fd: int,
707	        parent_key: str,
708	        display: Path,
709	        children: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
710	    ) -> None:
711	        for name, key in sorted(children.get(parent_key, ())):
712	            child_display = display / name
713	            descriptor = self._open_checked(
714	                parent_fd, child_display.name, child_display,
715	                *self.directories[key][1:],
716	            )
717	            try:
718	                self._verify_children(
719	                    descriptor, key, child_display, children
720	                )
721	            finally:
722	                os.close(descriptor)
723	
724	    def _descend(self, parts: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
725	        # Start from the root descriptor held open since before the
726	        # lookup: it pins the confirmed root inode regardless of later
727	        # path changes.  Only intermediate children are opened here, and
728	        # each is closed before returning (the root descriptor itself is
729	        # owned by the export and must not be closed).
730	        self._check_root()
731	        cursor = self.root_fd
732	        display = self.root
733	        owned: list[int] = []
734	        try:
735	            for part in parts:
736	                display = display / part
737	                key = os.path.relpath(display, self.root).replace(os.sep, "/")
738	                expected = self.directories.get(key)
739	                if expected is None:
740	                    raise ExportError(
741	                        f"directory changed during export: {display} is "
742	                        f"not part of the scanned tree"
743	                    )
744	                cursor = self._open_checked(cursor, part, display, *expected[1:])
745	                owned.append(cursor)
746	        finally:
747	            for descriptor in owned:
748	                os.close(descriptor)
749	
750	    def _open_checked(
751	        self,
752	        parent_fd: int,
753	        name: str,
754	        display: Path,
755	        expected_dev: int,
756	        expected_inode: int,
757	    ) -> int:
758	        """Open one directory component, refusing any changed binding.
759	
760	        This is the copy-phase half of the shared confirmation rule: the
761	        directory was already confirmed during the lookup, so the binding
762	        must still carry the recorded identity, and failures are reported
763	        as happening during the export rather than the scan.
764	        """
765	        return _open_confirmed_directory(
766	            parent_fd,
767	            name,
768	            display,
769	            expected=(expected_dev, expected_inode),
770	            during_scan=False,
771	        )

774	# Open-relative-to-a-directory-descriptor support (openat/fstatat with
775	# dir_fd, O_NOFOLLOW, O_DIRECTORY) is provided by the module-level
776	# _O_NOFOLLOW / _O_DIRECTORY flags above.
777	
778	
779	def _hash_regular_file_at(
780	    directory_fd: int, name: str, path: Path
781	) -> tuple[str, int, int]:
782	    """Read one directory-relative file in full, pinned through the open.
783	
784	    The name is inspected with ``fstatat`` relative to the pinned
785	    directory descriptor and opened with ``openat`` plus
786	    ``O_NOFOLLOW``, so a symlink swapped in after the inspection cannot
787	    redirect the read (the open fails with ``ELOOP``) and the bytes can
788	    only come from an entry reached through the confirmed directory.
789	    The recorded identity is the ``fstatat`` result; the copy later
790	    independently re-pins the exact inode (including the fstat proof)
791	    before its bytes are streamed into the package, so this lookup
792	    deliberately does not prove the descriptor itself.  Any failure
793	    raises with the path and reason.  Returns ``(digest, device,
794	    inode)``.
795	
796	    The confirm/open rule and the chunked hashing come from
797	    :mod:`confirmed`, shared with import; only the export wording is
798	    assembled here.
799	    """
800	    try:
801	        before = confirmed.inspect_regular(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)
802	        descriptor = confirmed.open_without_follow(name, dir_fd=directory_fd)
803	    except confirmed.ConfirmationError as failure:
804	        raise _scan_file_error(failure, path) from failure
805	    try:
806	        digest = confirmed.hash_descriptor(descriptor)
807	    except OSError as error:
808	        raise ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {error}") from error
809	    return digest, before.st_dev, before.st_ino
810	
811	
812	def _scan_file_error(
813	    failure: confirmed.ConfirmationError, path: Path
814	) -> ExportError:
815	    """Translate a shared confirmation failure into the scan's wording."""
816	    if failure.stage is confirmed.ConfirmStage.INSPECT:
817	        if failure.reason is confirmed.ConfirmReason.ACCESS_ERROR:
818	            return ExportError(
819	                f"cannot inspect entry {path}: {failure.error}"
820	            )
821	        # A symlink or any other non-regular object at a name the walk
822	        # had just typed as a regular file: the entry changed.
823	        return ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: not a regular file")
824	    if failure.reason is confirmed.ConfirmReason.NOW_SYMLINK:
825	        return ExportError(
826	            f"cannot read source file {path}: path is now a symlink"
827	        )
828	    return ExportError(f"cannot read source file {path}: {failure.error}")

831	def _write_package(
832	    target: Path,
833	    classes: dict[str, str],
834	    members: list[dict[str, Any]],
835	    manifest: dict[str, Any],
836	    resolver: dict[str, tuple[Path, int, int]] | None = None,
837	    source_anchor: _SourceAnchor | None = None,
838	) -> None:
839	    """Write the ZIP atomically: lock the target name, stream to a temp file.
840	
841	    The target is never overwritten: an existing target is rejected and a
842	    temp file is used until the whole package has been written and fsynced,
843	    so a failure or interruption leaves no incomplete target.  An flock on
844	    a lock file next to the target serializes concurrent exports to the
845	    same path.
846	    """
847	    target = Path(target)
848	    parent = target.parent
849	    try:
850	        parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
851	    except OSError as error:
852	        raise ExportError(f"cannot create target directory {parent}: {error}") from error
853	
854	    lock_path = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.lock")
855	    try:
856	        lock_descriptor = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
857	    except OSError as error:
858	        raise ExportError(f"cannot lock target {target}: {error}") from error
859	
860	    temp_path: Path | None = None
861	    try:
862	        fcntl.flock(lock_descriptor, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
863	        if os.path.lexists(target):
864	            raise ExportError(f"target already exists: {target}")
865	
866	        fd, temp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(
867	            prefix=f".{target.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=parent
868	        )
869	        temp_path = Path(temp_name)
870	        try:
871	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
872	                _write_zip(
873	                    stream,
874	                    classes,
875	                    members,
876	                    manifest,
877	                    resolver,
878	                    source_anchor=source_anchor,
879	                )
880	                stream.flush()
